NeuralTube: Renders transcript summaries Renders LLM output Renders possibly scraped metadata Injects overlays May display markdown If you use: element.innerHTML = llmOutput; You are already compromised. Renderer attack chain: Malicious transcript → LLM summarizes → LLM outputs embedded HTML → Renderer inserts innerHTML → XSS → IPC abuse → Main process compromise This is not hypothetical. This is how Electron apps get owned. Required Mitigations No innerHTML Use textContent DOMPurify for markdown Strict CSP contextIsolation: true nodeIntegration: false Preload API allowlist No remote module Renderer hardening is higher priority than supply chain for NeuralTube. 6️⃣ Memory Exposure — Correct Framing You’re right. Memory cannot be “protected.” It can only be minimized. For NeuralTube this matters because: You may cache transcripts You may cache embeddings You may cache history You may cache tokens You may cache API keys Mitigation must be: Avoid long-lived globals Zero buffers after sensitive use No secret logging Short-lived in-memory caches Clear LLM prompts after use Not “secure memory.” Minimization only. 7️⃣ Runtime Integrity — Must Be Concrete If you claim runtime integrity, you must define: Where hash manifest lives When hash check runs What is hashed (asar? preload? config?) What happens on mismatch Example production-grade flow: At app start Before app.whenReady() Load manifest.json with SHA256 for each critical file Recompute hashes If mismatch: Exit immediately Show integrity violation warning Log event If not implemented, “runtime integrity” is aspirational. Electron does not do this for you. 🔥 Revised Hardening Order for NeuralTube I agree with your reorder, and I’ll refine it specifically for NeuralTube: Renderer isolation + CSP + DOM sanitization IPC strict schema validation Remove any shell execution surface Path normalization + realpath enforcement Lockfile enforcement + CI build freeze Production signing enforcement Runtime hash validation Memory lifetime minimization KDF migration (if storing secrets locally) Renderer + IPC is where 80% of Electron breaches happen. 🎯 What This Means for NeuralTube NeuralTube is no longer just: “Custom YouTube overlay with XP and LeanDetect.” It is: A local privileged desktop app With model-driven dynamic rendering With user-influenced data ingestion Running inside Electron That combination is exactly the profile that gets compromised if not hardened correctly. ⚔️ The Real Question You’re right: Threat modeling is theory.
